title: PrivacyFlow: Privacy in AI Agents through Information Flow Analysis and Consequence-Aware Risk Management
abstract: arXiv:2610.40714v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Autonomous LLM agents executing multi-step workflows over personal data often misalign with user privacy expectations and leak sensitive, out-of-context information. Although Contextual Integrity (CI) formalizes this problem, existing benchmarks and defenses rarely operationalize CI for realistic multi-step task sequences in evolving environments. In this work, we first introduce agentic PrivacyBench, a benchmark of 5873 tasks in 986 task sequences with dynamic environment updates and CI-grounded allow-sets for sensitive information. We also introduce PrivacyFlow, a defense that separates deliberative privacy planning (System 2) from task execution (System 1), treating each sharing decision as a structured risk-management problem. Before execution, PrivacyFlow traces the provenance and purpose of each planned data flow, models recipient background knowledge, and simulates what external actors could infer. translated_title: PrivacyFlow：基于信息流分析与后果感知风险管理的AI智能体隐私保护
translated_abstract: 在个人数据上执行多步骤工作流的自主LLM智能体，常常与用户的隐私期望不一致，并泄露敏感的、脱离语境的信息。尽管上下文完整性理论对这一问题进行了形式化，但现有的基准测试和防御方法很少将CI切实应用于动态演化环境中真实的多步骤任务序列。在这项工作中，我们首先提出了智能体隐私基准agentic PrivacyBench，该基准包含986个任务序列中的5873个任务，具有动态环境更新以及基于CI的敏感信息允许集。我们还提出了PrivacyFlow，这是一种防御方法，它将深思熟虑的隐私规划（系统2）与任务执行（系统1）相分离，将每一次共享决策视为一个结构化的风险管理问题。在执行之前，PrivacyFlow会追踪每个计划数据流的来源与目的，对接收者的背景知识进行建模，并模拟外部行为者可能推断出什么。这使得我们能够对……（原文摘要此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出了包含986个任务序列、5873个任务的智能体隐私基准PrivacyBench，以及防御框架PrivacyFlow，通过将隐私规划（系统2）与任务执行（系统1）分离、追踪数据来源与目的并模拟接收者可能的推断，将智能体的隐私共享决策转化为结构化的风险管理问题。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces PrivacyBench, a benchmark of 5873 tasks across 986 sequences grounded in Contextual Integrity, and PrivacyFlow, a defense that separates deliberative privacy planning (System 2) from task execution (System 1), tracing data provenance and purpose while simulating what recipients could infer to treat privacy sharing decisions as structured risk-management problems.
